Each candidate is scored by running it in giri, a Go SSA interpreter, on 50 test vectors. It must return the reference result on every vector, and leave xs unchanged. Among correct candidates, a lower abstract cost (the number of SSA instructions executed over all vectors) scores higher, and any correct candidate scores above any incorrect one. The only import allowed is math/bits. Keep the function's name and signature.
responses:
## Proposed change: index through array pointers to drop per-access bounds checks

Each constant-index access `xs[k]` on a slice compiles to its own bounds check plus a load address computation. The branch ladder performs many such accesses, so most of the executed SSA cost is likely in those checks rather than in the `OnesCount64` calls themselves. Converting the slice to a fixed-size array pointer (`(*[N]uint64)(xs)`, Go 1.17+) performs a single length check, after which constant indices into the array need no further checks.

Two earlier attempts that only added `_ = xs[k]` hints scored lower (3.0565 in D2), so I'm using the array-pointer form instead, which removes the checks entirely rather than hinting at them. Attempts 1–3 all reported identical cost (3567), so I expect this to be the first change that actually moves the count, but I can't confirm that without running it.

I'm changing two blocks: the 16-word peel and the 8-word block. The 4-word block is left alone to keep the diff small.
